summary: Hae-ju Sunim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University under Zhongxin Jiang and completed her MA under Kemo Jin in 1982. In 2010, she was a Director at the University of Freiburg.

Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Shizuoka High School and the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University, and Toyo Bunko.

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who completed his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1973) and founded the Eastern Institute (Toho Gakuin).

Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University, and CASS, studying under Xianlin Ji. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2012).

Hajime Sakurabe (1925–2012) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his undergraduate and PhD degrees at Otani University, studying under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, and later served there as a professor (1971–1986).

Hajime Tanabe (1885–1962) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and in Germany under Heidegger, Rickert, and Husserl. A disciple of Kitaro Nishida, he taught at Tohoku University and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku (1686–1769) was a Buddhist figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan around 1708 and under Hakuyūshi around 1710–1711. He taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui (1882–1963) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and in Europe, he held posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, and Nagoya universities, and served as Komazawa University president (1941).

Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani (1885–1973) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure. He studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under Sogaku Harada, Genpo Tsuyama, and Bokusan Nishiari, among others. He founded Sanbo Zen in 1954.

Hakuyu Hadano (1916–1989) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He spent his academic career at Tohoku University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026).
Halina Marlewicz is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Tadeusz Pobożniak. She holds a post as professor at Jagiellonian University (attested 1996).
Halina Safarewiczowa (1904–1980) was a linguist. She studied at Vilnius University (~1923–1927) and held a post at Jagiellonian University from around 1946 to 1974.

Halle O'Neal specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011) and serves as Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Hallvard Kåre Kuløy (1941–2001) worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as an officer at UNICEF (1972–1978, 1980–1984), edited the journal Kailash (~1973), and founded Orchid Press and Bibliotheca Himalayica in 1982.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated in Sri Lanka, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Edinburgh (PhD 1963). He headed the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990) and was vice president of the Pali Text Society (1984–1990).

Hana Preinhaelterová (1938–2018) was an Indologist and linguist. She studied under Dušan Zbavitel, Visva-Bharati University, and Charles University, where she later served as Professor of Indology (Bengali) from around 1990 to 2005.

Handrio Nurhan works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a BA at Soka University of America (2011–2015), an MA at Texas Tech University (2016–2018), and a PhD at Boston University in 2018.
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He is attested as a faculty member at Haverford College in 2009 and 2019.

Hanna Havnevik is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held a professorship at the University of Oslo (attested 2006–2008), where she later became Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
